look_here_first: LOOK FIRST at the mature anthocarp: it is glabrous with five broadly rounded ribs and smooth grooves (sulci). Next inspect the relatively large petaloid perianth (about 4–7 mm) and usually five exserted stamens. Narrow leaves alone are not diagnostic.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Calvin-approved Nyctaginaceae source-pool genus roadmap and completed Boerhavia scientific review in content/taxa/Nyctaginaceae/family.json
project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO records Texas as native at state scale; no project target-zone three-county PASS was established in completed review. Photo geography is not county occurrence evidence.

best_field_traits: Opposite narrow linear to lanceolate leaves on a perennial with branching stems; vegetative shape alone can overlap congeners.
Mature anthocarps about 2.5–3.5 mm, glabrous, broadly rounded ribs and smooth sulci.
Perianth about 4–7 mm, usually five stamens projecting beyond it; confirm reproductive structures rather than flower color.

comparisons.key_distinctions: B. linearifolia has glabrous fruits with broadly rounded ribs and smooth grooves; B. erecta has sharper ribs and a different fruit apex, while B. coccinea has stalked-glandular fruit hairs. Confirm perianth and exserted stamens as supporting traits; do not identify by leaf narrowness alone.
